key_insight: The paper localizes phase-field fracture solves to a small moving crack-tip patch by condensing the inactive exterior with a reusable Schur complement, cutting cost while preserving accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster large-scale fracture simulations in brittle solids, making adaptive phase-field methods more practical for quasi-static, dynamic, and 3D crack-growth problems.
method: Adaptively refine/coarsen a patch around the crack tip instead of solving the full domain every iteration.
Eliminate the inactive exterior with a Schur complement and reuse its factorization while the patch stays fixed.
Freeze the phase field in the exterior to reduce repeated work, with only a small approximation in the crack wake.
evidence_signal: Across quasi-static, branching, mixed-mode, and multi-crack tests, the method matched reference solutions with global differences below 0.5% and achieved wall-time speedups up to 22.8x as the domain doubled.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the patch remaining a good approximation of the evolving crack zone; freezing the exterior phase field may be less reliable when damage spreads rapidly.
paper_title: Adaptive Crack-Tip Localization of Phase-Field Fracture Computations
